questions.explanation: GDPR is the General Data Protection Regulation, a European Union law focused on data protection and privacy.

questions.stem: Which GDPR principle requires collecting only the data that is absolutely necessary?
questions.explanation: Data minimisation insists on collecting only the data that is absolutely necessary.

questions.stem: What does the GDPR principle of purpose limitation mean?
options: Data must be deleted after one year
Only one department may process personal data
Data must be stored within the EU
Data can only be used for specific, clearly stated reasons
Data must be encrypted at rest
questions.explanation: Purpose limitation means personal data can only be used for specific, clearly stated reasons.

questions.stem: Which GDPR principle mandates that data should not be kept longer than necessary?
questions.explanation: Storage limitation mandates that data should not be kept longer than necessary.

questions.stem: Under GDPR, which principle places responsibility on organisations to ensure all the other principles are adhered to?
questions.explanation: Accountability places the responsibility on organisations to ensure all the principles are adhered to and personal data is managed compliantly and ethically.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the individual rights that GDPR introduced?
options: The right to free cloud storage
The right to sell personal data
The right to unlimited data retention
questions.explanation: GDPR empowered individuals with rights to access, rectify and erase their data, data portability and the right to be forgotten.

questions.stem: What does the privacy-by-design approach spurred by GDPR involve?
options: Publishing all data processing code as open source
Outsourcing data protection to third parties
Embedding data protection measures into product design and service delivery, including data minimisation and appointing Data Protection Officers
Storing all personal data on paper
Restricting products to EU customers only
questions.explanation: Privacy by design embeds data protection into product design and service delivery, with strategies like data minimisation and appointing Data Protection Officers.

questions.stem: Which company was fined 746 million euros under GDPR in 2021?
questions.explanation: Amazon was fined 746 million euros in 2021; Instagram was fined 405 million euros in 2022.

questions.stem: Why has GDPR had a global influence beyond the European Union?
options: Because the United Nations adopted it as a treaty
Because it replaced all national privacy laws worldwide
Because it is enforced by the World Trade Organisation
Because it only applies to companies headquartered in the EU
Because it applies to all organisations dealing with the data of EU citizens, forcing companies worldwide to adjust their practices
questions.explanation: GDPR applies to all organisations handling EU citizens' data, so companies worldwide had to comply, and it catalysed similar regulations elsewhere.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the main GDPR violations leading to fines?
options: Using open-source software without a licence review
Lack of transparency about data practices
questions.explanation: The main violations cited are transparency, child data protection, cross-border issues, data breaches, data minimisation and consent; software licensing is not among them.
